variants.mechanism: Two-leaf rotary fan per side; lateral engine shoulders above its proposed folded corridor.
variants.direction:
L63. The main body gently widens rearward into a pair of compact tapered motor shoulders at approximately the original upper-engine height. Each shoulder has a long inward-sloping leading transition and a short polygonal nozzle housing at the back; the engine body is mostly integrated into the aft side, not a separate suspended tube. A clear angular change of plane links the relatively slim body behind the collar to the wider aft power section. Keep the native flank fan relief on the main central body, terminating before the sober shoulder service panels.
Spoiler: a low single TRANSVERSE structural cap across the aft shoulder tops, with a very shallow swept/chevron plan outline and downturned clipped ends integrated directly into the shoulders. No high arch or thin posts; any under-cap clearance is local at the stern, not a longitudinal roof recess. It is a reworked native transverse part.
Wings: two broad angular fan leaves per side, both clipped at their outer tips, the leading leaf slightly longer and the trailing leaf visibly overlapping beneath. Preserve native fan-like character while simplifying to two functional sections. Stowed packet runs beneath the motor shoulders. Overall impression: a coherent Liberty fighter with a wider, lower-spread power section, an unmistakable original collar and a restrained horizontal stern. Label L63.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / faithful native-ship redesign.
Create ONE carefully designed concept sheet for Freelancer's li_pir_elite. This is a functional fighter designed by a fictional breakaway Liberty shipyard. Its defining identity is the ORIGINAL THREE-RIB COLLAR behind the ORIGINAL COCKPIT. The Art Deco / Empire decorative panels complement its engineering. Use the actual source ship references, not any previous AI concept.

ONE PRINCIPAL ARCHITECTURAL CHANGE: relocate the original vertical aft engine stack into TWO COMPACT LATERAL ENGINE SHOULDERS, one left and one right at the rear, with both thrust axes parallel and aft-facing. Rebuild the connected aft body, spoiler attachments and folding-wing clearance as consequences of this one change. There is NO remaining centerline vertical engine stack and NO third engine. The new engines may be comparable in size for the paired installation; the collar and cockpit remain unchanged.

REFERENCE ROLES:
1. Original li_pir_elite cockpit/collar, immutable: copy its real low rounded glass capsule, original pane boundaries, thin metal frames, shell and original proportions. Preserve the three angular stepped transverse collar ribs, their sharp outer contours, visible spacing and forward projection. They must stand visibly free of the main hull. No new brow, hood or cap hiding any of these ribs. No elongated new nose, oversized canopy or cabin redesign.
2. Actual native pirate ship: PRIMARY shape and material language. Keep its longitudinal central body, inclined angular side faces, simple closed top, separate planar folding leaves and compact functional fighter scale. Its original vertical engine location is deliberately superseded.
3. Actual native non-pirate li_elite: understand original coherent construction and proportions beneath the color. Do NOT copy faction insignia or turn the whole concept pale white. This is the SAME ship family, not a generic jet or a new alien craft.
4. Native LI colored wing-motion reference: gives front-side roots, inclined wing plane and backward rotational nesting, NOT final leaf count or display colors. The concept uses TWO complete moving leaves per side instead of native three, four moving leaves total.
5. Native isolated stern components: distinguish real polygonal engine nozzles from spoiler and yellow hardpoint plates. Use the functional polygonal engine/exhaust vocabulary, but reposition into the specified lateral shoulders. Yellow mounting squares are NOT engines and must not substitute for exhausts.

CONSTRUCTION AND PROPORTION:
Keep cockpit and collar at their native relative size; body length stays close to native. Keep the central body relatively compact; gain WIDTH at the REAR through its attached engine shoulders, not by swelling the whole hull into a rectangular slab. From behind the collar, designed broad chamfered hull planes transition into the two short solid engine housings. They are close-set load-bearing parts of the aft body, not disconnected pods on arms and not giant cylinders. Each has ONE credible aft-facing deep polygonal nozzle with a visible rim and dark interior. Two nozzles, horizontally separated, must be clearly seen in REAR view. Maintain useful volume and angular fighter proportions. No open skeleton, pipes, radial disc engines or added towers.

Central roof remains CLOSED and broadly flat; the cargo doors are flush surface seams, not a recessed trench. No central roof slot, two high longitudinal walls, raised obelisks or sunken hatch. Retain clearance for the hatch between and ahead of the aft structure; do not mount a fin over it.

The spoiler is a modest functional stern piece attached to those engine shoulders, with its geometry specified below. Do not add a separate tall dorsal fin, twin tails or independent ornamental crown. This study must remain about the rearranged power section and readable native collar.

FOLDING WINGS:
Exactly TWO substantial separate polygonal leaves on each side, with real thickness, separate free tips, a visible overlap edge and compact solid rotary roots behind/below the collar. They spread in flight and rotate backward/inward into a full-size nested packet beside the LOWER hull. Engine shoulders sit above this folding corridor, not inside it; engine nozzles are aft of it. No fixed monolithic delta with decorative segmentation, third leaf, exposed rods or huge hinge discs. In STOWED retain identical full-size leaf shapes and rotate/overlap them, never shrink them. This proposes a new two-leaf mechanism; do not invent telescoping movement.

MATERIAL AND PIRATE CHARACTER:
Use native li_pir_elite muted red-brown, ochre and restrained pale fan decoration. Surfaces are maintained, structurally complete and operational, with restrained edge wear and a few subtly different replacement panels. No wreck damage, torn plating, missing ribs, extensive rust, heavy grime or visible chains. Fictional separatist identity comes from an alternative engineering arrangement. Native side-panel ornamental frieze ends at the new shoulder housing; plainer service panels continue across the motor casing. Give the collar visual priority. Keep original-game medium detail, strong planar shapes and clean readable material blocks. No cathedral ornaments, gilded palace sculpture, Confederate flag, skulls or spikes.

SHEET:
Pale grey background. Large front-side three-quarter view, nose LEFT, mild perspective with long lens; keep the collar exposed and cockpit normal-sized. Include a clear medium REAR THREE-QUARTER view exposing BOTH lateral engine nozzles. Smaller FRONT / SIDE / TOP and STOWED top view. Same exact design across views. Prioritize coherent massing, real two-leaf overlap and the engine arrangement over decorative microdetail. Labels only ID and view names; no explanatory paragraphs.
SPECIFIC VARIANT:
L63. The main body gently widens rearward into a pair of compact tapered motor shoulders at approximately the original upper-engine height. Each shoulder has a long inward-sloping leading transition and a short polygonal nozzle housing at the back; the engine body is mostly integrated into the aft side, not a separate suspended tube. A clear angular change of plane links the relatively slim body behind the collar to the wider aft power section. Keep the native flank fan relief on the main central body, terminating before the sober shoulder service panels.
Spoiler: a low single TRANSVERSE structural cap across the aft shoulder tops, with a very shallow swept/chevron plan outline and downturned clipped ends integrated directly into the shoulders. No high arch or thin posts; any under-cap clearance is local at the stern, not a longitudinal roof recess. It is a reworked native transverse part.
Wings: two broad angular fan leaves per side, both clipped at their outer tips, the leading leaf slightly longer and the trailing leaf visibly overlapping beneath. Preserve native fan-like character while simplifying to two functional sections. Stowed packet runs beneath the motor shoulders. Overall impression: a coherent Liberty fighter with a wider, lower-spread power section, an unmistakable original collar and a restrained horizontal stern. Label L63.

observations: REAR 3/4 clearly shows exactly two horizontally separated polygonal nozzles in compact integrated stern shoulders; the former vertical pair is absent.
Three collar flanges remain visually prominent and uncovered. Cabin retains native pane arrangement broadly, but proportions across raster views are not exact.
Center roof is closed, with flush hatch seams; short raised motor shoulders are localized aft rather than forming a full longitudinal trench.
Two fan leaves per side are legible; STOWED illustrates nesting below the shoulders. Actual leaf shapes/axes/clearance are not numerically validated.
Rear cap is low and tied to engine shoulders. Surface wear is moderate and the native side decoration ends at plainer motor casings.
The overall composition is intentionally close to native LI; greater silhouette divergence is concentrated in the stern.
Extra yellow equipment pads are illustrative and do not authorize new hardpoints.
modeling_constraints: Use native cabin and collar mesh unchanged.
New two-engine shoulder arrangement and two-leaf animation require geometry/HP/clearance authoring.
Keep closed center roof and complete cargo volume; source baydoor sweep is not proven by this sheet.

variants.mechanism: Two-leaf rotary fan per side; upper rear motor shoulders and a lower folding corridor.
variants.direction:
L64. Explore a more pronounced TWO-STEP transition from the slim body behind the native collar to short HIGHER rear motor shoulders. The rear half widens through one crisp diagonal outward step; each motor casing rises modestly above the central roof only in the last rear third, its top plane sloping down toward the front. House the two nozzles in these upper left/right rear shoulders, horizontally paired, not stacked. This produces a compact squared-off upper stern and an articulated lower waist, without a giant full-width box or long twin booms. The central flat roof remains filled and level, not a trench between long walls: shoulder rises are short, aft-local volumes only.
Spoiler: one continuous shallow angular aft visor integrated into the top/rear of those shoulders, with a clipped center projecting slightly REARWARD and thick tapered end returns. It reads as the shaped protective finishing piece of the motor group, not a fin and not a new decorative superstructure. Keep this piece low; native collar remains the visual signature.
Wings: two more swept polygonal leaves per side with one long clipped leading blade and a shorter, broader inner leaf creating a pronounced stepped trailing edge. Separate tips and real overlap, not one delta. Their compact roots remain low near the front-side body; stowed both full-size plates nest below the short raised motor shoulders. Keep a calmer inset ornamental panel on the main flank and plain service panels on the new casing, with only subtle repaint differences. Label L64.

observations: REAR 3/4 clearly confirms a horizontal pair of aft polygonal nozzles; their housings are integrated into short raised rear shoulders.
The step from central flank into engine casings and the lowered body below them gives a stronger change of volume than L63.
Native three-rib collar is exposed, without the earlier brow. Cabin remains recognizable but raster proportions and contour accuracy are limited.
The central roof is closed with flush hatch outline. The short gap beneath the aft visor is a local stern clearance, not the rejected full-length center trough.
Two swept wing leaves per side are apparent; TOP STOWED suggests backward folding, but leaf angles/hidden shape and clearance are not validated.
TOP is oriented nose-down, unlike L63; all art views remain illustrative rather than measured.
Extra mounting pads and exact engine hardware shown by the generator are not an approved hardpoint configuration.
modeling_constraints: Reuse native cabin and collar geometry unchanged.
New lateral engine layout needs proper nozzle bodies, HPs and structural clearance design.
Verify wing folding under shoulders and native baydoor clearance in actual geometry.

accepted_for_trial: Two compact lateral engine shoulders as the single architectural change. Native collar and cockpit priority. No strong wear. Two foldable sections per side, flat closed roof.
scope: Two offline concept trials after rejection of L59–L62. No prior AI artwork used as input. Proposed new engine layout and two-leaf mechanics are unvalidated.
